findings.quote: Europa has an icy shell, so it is not mostly rock.
findings.problem: Europa is mostly rock. NASA describes an iron core and a rocky mantle under a water and ice layer roughly 100 km deep, on a moon of radius 1,561 km; its mean density is 3,010 kg/m3, close to rock and far above ice. An icy surface does not make a moon 'not mostly rock'. The same error is in Core Concept: 'Many moons are not mostly rock. Europa, a moon of Jupiter, has an icy shell'. The example's conclusion still holds through Phobos and Ganymede, but its first step teaches a false fact and a false inference (surface ice means not mostly rock). Ganymede (1,940 kg/m3) or Callisto (1,830 kg/m3) would fit the claim.
findings.source: NASA Science, Europa Facts (science.nasa.gov/jupiter/jupiter-moons/europa/europa-facts); NASA NSSDCA Jovian Satellite Fact Sheet (nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/joviansatfact.html)

findings.quote: a tiny but very dense ball about $20$ km across, or a black hole.
findings.problem: Black hole is used as an end state of massive stars here and as part of the answer in Example #7, but the lesson never says what a black hole is (a collapsed object whose gravity is so strong that not even light escapes). Neutron star, white dwarf and the other end states get a meaning; black hole is named only, so a student cannot recognize one from a description, which the lesson's classification goal needs. No prerequisite lesson is named.
findings.source: content-checklist L25 and L26; lesson-style-guide Teaching completeness

findings.quote: Scientists also sort stars into the spectral classes O, B, A, F, G, K, and M, from hottest to coolest. The Sun is class G.
findings.problem: This paragraph has four sentences, over the one-to-three-sentence limit. Other paragraphs also run over: 'Galaxies have three common shapes' (4), 'The giant planets are much larger' (4), 'A **natural satellite**, or moon' (4), 'Many moons are not mostly rock' (5), 'A **comet** is a small body of ice' (4), and 'The gas and dust form a glowing cloud' (4).
